Let \(p=503\), so the residue classes defining \(S_r\) are modulo \(p-1=502\).

Write \(10000\) in base \(503\):
\[
10000=19\cdot 503+443.
\]
For \(k=a\cdot503+b\), where \(0\le b<503\), Lucas’s theorem gives
\[
\binom{10000}{k}\equiv \binom{19}{a}\binom{443}{b}\pmod{503}.
\]
Thus the binomial coefficient is \(0\pmod{503}\) whenever \(a>19\) or \(b>443\).

Also, since \(503\equiv1\pmod{502}\),
\[
k=a\cdot503+b\equiv a+b\pmod{502}.
\]
For the potentially nonzero terms, \(0\le a\le19\) and \(0\le b\le443\), so
\[
0\le a+b\le462<502.
\]
Therefore, for \(0\le r\le462\),
\[
S_r\equiv\sum_{a+b=r}\binom{19}{a}\binom{443}{b}
=\binom{462}{r}\pmod{503}
\]
by Vandermonde’s identity. Since \(462<503\), none of the binomial coefficients \(\binom{462}{r}\) is divisible by \(503\).

For \(463\le r\le501\), there are no potentially nonzero terms with \(a+b=r\), so
\[
S_r\equiv0\pmod{503}.
\]
The number of such indices is
\[
501-463+1=39.
\]

-2\sum_{n=4}^{\infty}\frac{n+1}{3^n}
\right].
\end{aligned}

\[

=\frac{7}{54}.
